content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To choose a cut of meat for stews, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Note the price per pound of chuck roast (2 minutes)
Step 2. Compare the fat content of brisket versus shank (10 minutes)
Step 3. Read about the connective tissue in oxtail (15 minutes)
Step 4. Look up the gelatin content of beef cheeks (10 minutes)
Step 5. Research the differences between grass-fed and grain-fed beef (30 minutes)
Step 6. Check the availability of pre-cut stew meat (5 minutes)
Step 7. Ask the butcher for a custom trim (5 minutes)
Step 8. Weigh the selected meat portion (2 minutes)
Step 9. Inspect the marbling on the short ribs (4 minutes)
Step 10. Decide on the total budget for the meal (10 minutes)
Step 11. Read a review of local organic farms (20 minutes)
Step 12. Evaluate the thickness of the silver skin (3 minutes)
Step 13. Look up a recipe for classic Guinness stew (15 minutes)
Step 14. Determine the required cooking time for each cut (10 minutes)
Step 15. Check the "sell-by" dates on the packages (2 minutes)
Step 16. Verify the country of origin on the label (1 minute)
Step 17. Smell the meat for freshness (30 seconds)
Step 18. Assess the color of the muscle fibers (3 minutes)
Step 19. Consider the size of the slow cooker (5 minutes)
Step 20. Consult a culinary textbook on braising (1 hour)
Step 21. Place the meat in a shopping basket (30 seconds)
Step 22. Calculate the number of servings needed (5 minutes)
Step 23. Ask about the age of the cattle (5 minutes)
Step 24. Find a parking spot at the butcher shop (10 minutes)
Step 25. Check for any meat recalls online (15 minutes)
Step 26. Inquire about the butcher's favorite cut (5 minutes)
Step 27. Examine the texture of the lean meat (2 minutes)
Step 28. Search for a discount coupon (5 minutes)
Step 29. Decide if bone-in or boneless is better (5 minutes)
Step 30. Check the butcher's hours of operation (2 minutes)
Step 31. Look for a clean cutting board in the shop (2 minutes)
Step 32. Press the meat to check for firmness (30 seconds)
Step 33. Compare the color of various cuts (5 minutes)
Step 34. Estimate the shrinkage during cooking (5 minutes)
Step 35. Finalize the choice of the meat cut (1 minute)
Step 36. Look at the butcher's display case (5 minutes)
Step 37. Read the nutritional information (5 minutes)
Step 38. Calculate the protein content (5 minutes)
Step 39. Evaluate the ratio of meat to bone (5 minutes)
Step 40. Look for the USDA inspection stamp (2 minutes)
Step 41. Consider the flavor profile of the fat (5 minutes)
Step 42. Ask the butcher to wrap the meat (3 minutes)
Step 43. Request a specific weight of meat (2 minutes)
Step 44. Check for any visible bruising (2 minutes)
Step 45. Ask for storage recommendations (3 minutes)
Step 46. Look at the butcher's knife skills (5 minutes)
Step 47. Check the temperature of the refrigerated case (2 minutes)
Step 48. Pay for the selected meat (3 minutes)
Step 49. Observe the moisture level in the package (2 minutes)
Step 50. Determine the flavor profile of the stew (20 minutes)
Step 51. Read the instructions for the pressure cooker (15 minutes)
Step 52. Walk into the meat department (1 minute)
Step 53. Ask if the meat was previously frozen (2 minutes)
Step 54. Double-check the price tag (1 minute)
Step 55. Check the salt content of pre-marinated options (5 minutes)
Step 56. Ask for a sample of the meat (5 minutes)
Step 57. Search for the butcher's shop on a map (5 minutes)
Step 58. Identify the best herbs to pair with the meat (10 minutes)
Step 59. Compare the quality of different brands (15 minutes)
Step 60. Check for any gristle in the cut (4 minutes)
